what_it_is.prose: The jet-based kamikaze drone system is an indigenous Indian programme to develop a high-speed jet-powered loitering munition (kamikaze drone) capable of striking high-value targets at speeds far exceeding propeller-driven loitering munitions like the Switchblade or Harop. The programme involves DRDO and Israeli Aerospace Industries (IAI), leveraging Israel's experience with the Harop and Harpy loitering munitions. The system fills a critical operational gap between expensive cruise missiles (like BrahMos) and slower propeller-driven loitering munitions, providing a relatively affordable high-speed precision strike capability. The jet-powered drone can be launched from ground-based or vehicle-mounted launchers, loiter in a target area, and then accelerate to terminal attack speed when a target is identified. The system is intended for the Indian Army and Air Force for strikes against radar sites, command posts, air defence systems, and other high-value targets. The programme is in the development/procurement phase.

faq.question: What is a jet-based kamikaze drone?
faq.answer: A jet-based kamikaze drone is a jet-powered loitering munition that can loiter over a target area and then accelerate to high speed for a terminal attack on a designated target. Unlike propeller-driven loitering munitions (which are slower but longer-enduring), jet-powered variants offer much higher speed (~400–600 km/h) but shorter endurance (~30–60 minutes). They fill the gap between cruise missiles and propeller loitering munitions, providing affordable high-speed precision strikes.

faq.question: Is this the same as the IAI Harop?
faq.answer: The Indian programme draws on Israeli Aerospace Industries (IAI) experience with the Harop and Harpy loitering munitions, but is being developed as a distinct system tailored to Indian requirements. The Indian variant may incorporate indigenous components and modifications. Whether it will be called Harop or given a distinct Indian name has not been confirmed.

faq.question: What is the jet-based kamikaze drone system?
faq.answer: It is a rapidly developed Indian loitering munition concept that adds a jet engine to a kamikaze drone to achieve speeds and strike ranges beyond typical propeller-driven loitering munitions. Both DRDO and the Indian Air Force are advancing jet-powered loitering munition designs for deep-strike roles.

faq.question: Who is developing this system and for what role?
faq.answer: DRDO is developing a stealth jet-powered swarm loitering munition with a reported 300-600 km strike range, while the Indian Air Force is separately pursuing indigenous kamikaze drones with industry partners. These systems provide precision deep-strike options for peacetime coercion and wartime effect.
